schema.title: C4OS Grill Question 040 - Plugin Backend Registration Boundary

questions.label: How should C4OS expose plugin backend capabilities?
questions.help: Recommended: C4OS exposes backend tools through one app-owned tool gateway, while plugins declare the tools they contribute or consume. This preserves approval policy and runtime discovery.
options: App-owned tool gateway with plugin-declared tool contributions and consumers
Each plugin gets its own Tauri command namespace
Plugins call any registered Tauri command directly
Only bundled plugins can expose backend capabilities
Other

questions.label: Where should plugin tool contributions be declared?
questions.help: Recommended: declare C4OS app-tool contributions in agents/c4os.yaml, then bind them to implementation under the plugin's c4os/ code.
options: agents/c4os.yaml declares tools; plugin c4os/ code implements bindings
.codex-plugin/plugin.json declares all C4OS tools
Runtime discovers tools by scanning plugin code
Only core C4OS can declare tools
Other

questions.label: How should native backend registration work for marketplace plugins?
questions.help: Recommended: marketplace plugins can request app-tool bindings, but only preinstalled C4OS/Tauri native modules are loaded unless the user approves a signed/native install model later.
options: Marketplace plugins bind to preinstalled C4OS/Tauri native modules only
Marketplace plugins can ship and load native Tauri modules
Only bundled/default plugins can use native backend modules
No plugin can use native backend modules
Other

questions.label: Who owns approval policy for plugin-contributed tools?
questions.help: Recommended: C4OS owns default and maximum approval policy per tool; plugin manifests can request defaults but cannot silently widen authority.
options: C4OS owns default and maximum approval policy; plugins can request narrower defaults
Plugin manifest owns approval policy
User config owns all approval policy with no C4OS maximum
Runtime adapter owns approval policy
Other

questions.label: Notes or corrections
questions.help: Clarify Tauri tool discovery, native install security, signed plugin expectations, tool IDs, app-tool naming, or marketplace plugin limitations.
